note: The check has two halves and they came out differently. The work order status colours FAIL: every one of the nine statuses comes out a different colour in the search than it does in the rest of the app, and three change colour completely. The part stock colours PASS: all twelve parts checked match exactly.
evidence:
MEASURED 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 on build v26.36.7-29ca209, by reading the colour the product itself applies rather than judging shades by eye, and by comparing the SAME record on both screens.

PART A - WORK ORDER STATUS COLOURS: FAILED.
Each status was isolated on the Work Orders list with its own filter for the customer ZZAUTOTEST Fibridge Commercial, the work order number was written down, and that same work order was then found in the search.
  Estimate         S9160-17669   list blue           search a different blue
  Approved         S9160-17657   list teal green     search a different green
  In Progress      S9160-17660   list GREEN          search ORANGE
  Review           S9160-17662   list orange         search a different orange
  Complete         S9160-17667   list orange         search a different orange
  Invoiced         S9160-17668   list GREEN          search GREY
  Paid             S9160-17661   list teal green     search a different green
  Declined         S9160-17665   list RED            search ORANGE
  Imported         no such work order exists on this branch; the two colours below come from the product's own colour tables, not from the screen: the rest of the app gives it deep purple, the search gives it grey.
Not one of the nine matches. And because the search keeps only four colours of its own, In Progress, Review, Complete and Declined all land on the same orange, so a declined work order looks the same as a finished one.

PART B - PART STOCK COLOURS: PASSED.
On Parts then Inventory, the Supply menu was set to Under-supplied, Well-supplied and Over-supplied in turn, the colour under Total Quantity and the part number written down, and each number then typed into the search and read off the Parts tab. Under-supplied is red, well-supplied green, over-supplied orange. Twelve parts were checked, four per level, and all twelve match on both the colour and the number - including a part holding minus one, which reads minus one in both places. The part row uses the same badge as the rest of the app, which is exactly what is required, and shows the search is able to do it.

A WARNING FOR WHOEVER RE-RUNS PART B: three of these part numbers are carried by TWO different parts - LF3973, N000000001069 and P550848. Match the row by its description, not by the number alone, or you will read the wrong part and report a fault that is not there. It nearly happened twice here.

ONE THING THAT IS NOT A FAULT BUT IS WORTH ASKING ABOUT: the written requirement says a part at zero should be red. On this branch a part at zero is sometimes red and sometimes green, depending on the part's own minimum. Both screens agree with each other, so this is not a search fault; it is a question about the shared rule.

THIS CASE WAS CORRECTED THE SAME DAY, with the QA lead's go-ahead. Its earlier version listed fixed colours per status, taken from an older copy of the requirement document. The page read live no longer fixes any colour; it requires only that the search and the rest of the app agree. Both halves are now written out as a tester can actually run them.

Reported to the developers as SV-10186 - https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10186 (Part A only; Part B passes).
